t: Abandoned by his father's people as a child, Temüjin built a following through personal loyalty and alliances and by 1204 had defeated every rival on the Mongolian steppe.
As Genghis Khan from 1206 he replaced tribal loyalties with a decimal military system and commanders chosen for merit, bound to the khan and his family.
His campaigns against the Western Xia, the Jin and the Khwarazmian Empire killed millions and devastated China, Central Asia and Persia, while opening trade and exchange across Eurasia.
dyk: The Secret History of the Mongols, the main source for his youth, is often critical of its subject: it presents Genghis Khan as indecisive and as having a phobia of dogs, and it records that he killed his own half-brother.
ev: Temüjin is born to the Borjigin chieftain Yesügei and his wife Hö'elün; the year is disputed
He is defeated by his former sworn brother Jamukha at Dalan Baljut
He joins a Jin campaign against the Tatars and helps Toghrul to regain the lordship of the Kereit
Attacked by Toghrul and defeated at Qalaqaljid Sands, he regroups at Baljuna and overpowers the Kereit
An assembly at the source of the Onon River sees him formally adopt the title Genghis Khan
The Jin capital Zhongdu surrenders after a four-year campaign and is sacked
He invades the Khwarazmian Empire after the killing of his envoy
He dies in August while subduing the Western Xia, whose capital falls the following month

f.born: c. 1162 (historians also favour 1155 or 1167), at Delüün Boldog on the Onon River according to the Secret History of the Mongols; eldest child of Yesügei, a chieftain of the Borjigin clan, and Hö'elün
f.died: 18 or 25 August 1227, during the siege of the Western Xia capital Zhongxing, after months of illness following a fall from his horse; the exact cause is disputed
f.role: Khan of the Mongols (acclaimed by his followers before c. 1187); Genghis Khan, first khan of the Mongol Empire, 1206–1227
f.known: Uniting the tribes of the Mongolian steppe; founding the Mongol Empire; reorganising Mongol society into a decimal military system; the conquest of the Jin capital Zhongdu; the destruction of the Khwarazmian Empire; campaigns that killed millions; a trading system spanning Eurasia
